div.l: And pynnes . for to yeue faire wyues .
And certenly . he had hadhad a merye note .
Well couthe he syngen . ⁊and pleien on a rote .
Of yeddynges . he bar vtterly the pris .
His nek white . as is the flour delys .
Ther to he was stronge . as is a Champioıı̄un .
He knewe the tauerners . well in eủery toıı̄un .
And euery hostiler . ⁊and Tapster .
Bet than a lazar . or a begger .
For vn to suche . a worthi man as he .
Accordyd nought . as bi his faculte .
To haue wtith suche lazares acqueyntaūnce .
It is nought honest . it may noght auaūnce .
For to dele . with suche porayle .
But all wtith riche . ⁊and sellers of vitayle .
And ouer all there . as ꝓprofite schulde a ryse .
Curteis he was . ⁊and lowly of seruyse .
Ther nas no man . nowher so vertuous
He was the best begger . in his hous .
For though a wydewe . had noght a scho .
So plesaūnt was . his Inprincipio .
Yet wolde he haue . a ferthyng or he wente .
His purchas was well better . than his rente .
And rage he couthe . as it were a whelpe .
In louedayes . ther couthe he moche helpe .
For there was he noght . lik a cloister .
In a thredbare cope . lik is a poủere scoler .
But he was lik . a maister or a pope .
Of double worstede . was his semycope .
That rounded was as a belle . out of the presse .
Somwhat he lipsed . for his wantownesse .
To make his englysch . swete vp on his tonge .
And in harpyng . whan he had songe .
His yen twynkled . in his heed a right .
As don the sterres . in the frosty nyght .
This worthi lymytorur . was cleped huberd .
A Marchaūnt was þ̉ere . with a forked berd .
In motle . ⁊and high on hors he sat .
Vp on his heed . a flaundrisch beuere hat .
His botis clapsed . faire ⁊and fetisly .
His resons he spak . full solemply .
Schewyng alwaye . the encres of his wynyng .
He wolde the see . were kept for eny thyng .
Betwyxe Middelburgh . ⁊and Orwelle .
Well couthe he . in eschaunge scheeldis selle .
This worthi man . full well his witte bisette .
Ther wist no wight . that he was in dette .
